raw.title: Principal, Financial Crime and Regulatory Compliance
raw.description:
FARFETCH exists for the love of fashion. Our mission is to be the global platform for luxury fashion, connecting creators, curators and consumers.

We're a positive platform for good, bringing together an incredible creative community made up by our people, our partners and our customers. This community is at the heart of our business success. We welcome differences, empower individuality and celebrate diverse skills and perspectives, creating an inclusive environment for everyone. We are FARFETCH for All.

LEGAL, ETHICS AND COMPLIANCE

Working in close partnership, the Legal and Ethics & Compliance (E&C) teams operate as a strategic business area helping us navigate the complexities of a global business. The Legal team acts as guardians of our legal integrity, providing expert advice to protect our interests and manage risks.  Alongside them, the E&C team drives our commitment to doing business the right way by developing robust compliance frameworks, monitoring regulatory adherence, and fostering a strong culture of ethical conduct.

LONDON

Our London office is located in Old Street, London’s tech hub, and is home to a wide range of teams. Our open space is ideal for collaborative work and sharing ideas. We also have a large outdoor terrace, which is the perfect spot to have a team lunch or host events.

THE ROLE

The Principal, Financial Crime and Regulatory Compliance is a senior role responsible for building, scaling, and overseeing global AML and Sanctions compliance programs that protect the company from regulatory, financial, and reputational risk.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Program

  • Design and lead AML frameworks across multiple jurisdictions, including Due Diligence, and Suspicious Transaction Reporting.

  • Establish consistent governance standards, documentation requirements, and operational controls to ensure regulatory alignment across markets.

  • Identify emerging AML risk typologies and direct the development of analytic methods, and escalation criteria.

  • Conduct comprehensive enterprise-wide AML risk assessments and implement robust remediation plans to address identified vulnerabilities.

  • Serve as the principal liaison for internal audits, external regulatory examinations, and law enforcement inquiries related to money laundering.

    • Transaction Monitoring, Fraud & Ecosystem Defense

    • Design and manage Transaction Monitoring frameworks to identify suspicious activities and financial crime typologies across the global platform.

    • Extend Transaction Monitoring capabilities to function as a holistic defense mechanism, integrating preventative controls over fraud, Trust and Safety, and payment anomalies.

    • Support the design and operation of monitoring mechanisms for fraud, seller abuse, or related risk indicators, coordinating with internal functions as needed.

    • Partner with engineering and data teams to deploy advanced monitoring rules and real-time detection solutions to protect the platform's ecosystem.

      • Sanctions Compliance Management

      • Lead global sanctions screening for new and existing partners/customers and ensure compliance with U.S., U.K., E.U., and other applicable sanctions regimes.

      • Oversee sanctions system configuration, alert review procedures, and escalation protocols to maintain screening accuracy and defensibility.

      • Implement and manage comprehensive e-commerce sanctions controls beyond entity screening, including IP geolocation blocking, restricted delivery address logic, and cross-border shipping restrictions for high-risk regions.

      • Provide guidance to business teams on sanctions implications for customers, products, and market expansion.

      • Monitor real-time geopolitical developments and proactively update internal sanctions policies to mitigate emerging jurisdictional risks.

      • Establish ongoing testing and calibration routines for screening tools to minimize false positives and optimize tools.

        • Regulatory Advisory & Compliance Awareness

        • Continuously assess evolving legal and regulatory requirements across multiple global jurisdictions to ensure the compliance framework remains robust and current.

        • Provide strategic advice, interpretation, and counsel to business units and executive leadership on applicable AML, Sanctions, and Financial Crime obligations.

        • Design, implement, and oversee comprehensive compliance training and awareness programs tailored to relevant teams and departments, fostering a proactive culture of risk management.

          • Cross-Functional Compliance Support

          • Provide support across adjacent compliance domains including ESG reporting.

          • Act as a senior compliance advisor for major strategic initiatives, ensuring that financial crime controls are seamlessly embedded into new market launches and platform features.


WHO YOU ARE
  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field and progressive experience in Compliance, with strong exposure to AML, sanctions, or financial crime risk management and related compliance domains. Certifications like CAMS and CGSS are a plus.
  • Experienced in designing and scaling compliance programs across multiple jurisdictions and compliance areas.
  • Strong understanding of global regulatory frameworks related to AML and Sanctions.
  • Familiarity with ESG and sustainability reporting; CSRD experience is a plus.
  • Proven ability to build intelligence-driven monitoring programs and high-quality control environments.
  • Skilled stakeholder manager with excellent communication and influence capabilities.
  • Comfortable operating in fast-paced, evolving environments with complex global regulatory expectations.
  • Highly analytical, detail-oriented, and capable of driving cross-functional initiatives at senior levels.

REWARDS & BENEFITS
- Employee Pension Scheme 
- Flexible Benefits Program 
- Health Insurance & Critical Illness cover 
- Flexible work environment- Hybrid Model (3 days a week from the office, 2 days from home)

EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT & SCAM DISCLAIMER

  • EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT- Farfetch is an equal opportunities employer ensuring that all applicants are treated equally and fairly throughout our recruitment process. We are determined that no applicant experiences discrimination on the basis of sex, race, ethnicity, religion or belief, disability, age, gender identity, ancestry, sexual orientation, veteran status, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, or any other basis prohibited by applicable law. 

  • SCAM DISCLAIMER- It has come to our attention that there may be fraudulent activities involving individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent Farfetch in order to attract candidates to a SCAM. Please be aware that Farfetch does not conduct recruitment processes through messaging apps or any unofficial communication channels, other than our official careers website. raw.title: Principal, Financial Crime and Regulatory Compliance
raw.description:
FARFETCH exists for the love of fashion. Our mission is to be the global platform for luxury fashion, connecting creators, curators and consumers.

We're a positive platform for good, bringing together an incredible creative community made up by our people, our partners and our customers. This community is at the heart of our business success. We welcome differences, empower individuality and celebrate diverse skills and perspectives, creating an inclusive environment for everyone. We are FARFETCH for All.

LEGAL, ETHICS AND COMPLIANCE

Working in close partnership, the Legal and Ethics & Compliance (E&C) teams operate as a strategic business area helping us navigate the complexities of a global business. The Legal team acts as guardians of our legal integrity, providing expert advice to protect our interests and manage risks.  Alongside them, the E&C team drives our commitment to doing business the right way by developing robust compliance frameworks, monitoring regulatory adherence, and fostering a strong culture of ethical conduct.

LONDON

Our London office is located in Old Street, London’s tech hub, and is home to a wide range of teams. Our open space is ideal for collaborative work and sharing ideas. We also have a large outdoor terrace, which is the perfect spot to have a team lunch or host events.

THE ROLE

The Principal, Financial Crime and Regulatory Compliance is a senior role responsible for building, scaling, and overseeing global AML and Sanctions compliance programs that protect the company from regulatory, financial, and reputational risk.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Program

  • Design and lead AML frameworks across multiple jurisdictions, including Due Diligence, and Suspicious Transaction Reporting.

  • Establish consistent governance standards, documentation requirements, and operational controls to ensure regulatory alignment across markets.

  • Identify emerging AML risk typologies and direct the development of analytic methods, and escalation criteria.

  • Conduct comprehensive enterprise-wide AML risk assessments and implement robust remediation plans to address identified vulnerabilities.

  • Serve as the principal liaison for internal audits, external regulatory examinations, and law enforcement inquiries related to money laundering.

    • Transaction Monitoring, Fraud & Ecosystem Defense

    • Design and manage Transaction Monitoring frameworks to identify suspicious activities and financial crime typologies across the global platform.

    • Extend Transaction Monitoring capabilities to function as a holistic defense mechanism, integrating preventative controls over fraud, Trust and Safety, and payment anomalies.

    • Support the design and operation of monitoring mechanisms for fraud, seller abuse, or related risk indicators, coordinating with internal functions as needed.

    • Partner with engineering and data teams to deploy advanced monitoring rules and real-time detection solutions to protect the platform's ecosystem.

      • Sanctions Compliance Management

      • Lead global sanctions screening for new and existing partners/customers and ensure compliance with U.S., U.K., E.U., and other applicable sanctions regimes.

      • Oversee sanctions system configuration, alert review procedures, and escalation protocols to maintain screening accuracy and defensibility.

      • Implement and manage comprehensive e-commerce sanctions controls beyond entity screening, including IP geolocation blocking, restricted delivery address logic, and cross-border shipping restrictions for high-risk regions.

      • Provide guidance to business teams on sanctions implications for customers, products, and market expansion.

      • Monitor real-time geopolitical developments and proactively update internal sanctions policies to mitigate emerging jurisdictional risks.

      • Establish ongoing testing and calibration routines for screening tools to minimize false positives and optimize tools.

        • Regulatory Advisory & Compliance Awareness

        • Continuously assess evolving legal and regulatory requirements across multiple global jurisdictions to ensure the compliance framework remains robust and current.

        • Provide strategic advice, interpretation, and counsel to business units and executive leadership on applicable AML, Sanctions, and Financial Crime obligations.

        • Design, implement, and oversee comprehensive compliance training and awareness programs tailored to relevant teams and departments, fostering a proactive culture of risk management.

          • Cross-Functional Compliance Support

          • Provide support across adjacent compliance domains including ESG reporting.

          • Act as a senior compliance advisor for major strategic initiatives, ensuring that financial crime controls are seamlessly embedded into new market launches and platform features.


WHO YOU ARE
  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field and progressive experience in Compliance, with strong exposure to AML, sanctions, or financial crime risk management and related compliance domains. Certifications like CAMS and CGSS are a plus.
  • Experienced in designing and scaling compliance programs across multiple jurisdictions and compliance areas.
  • Strong understanding of global regulatory frameworks related to AML and Sanctions.
  • Familiarity with ESG and sustainability reporting; CSRD experience is a plus.
  • Proven ability to build intelligence-driven monitoring programs and high-quality control environments.
  • Skilled stakeholder manager with excellent communication and influence capabilities.
  • Comfortable operating in fast-paced, evolving environments with complex global regulatory expectations.
  • Highly analytical, detail-oriented, and capable of driving cross-functional initiatives at senior levels.

REWARDS & BENEFITS
- Employee Pension Scheme 
- Flexible Benefits Program 
- Health Insurance & Critical Illness cover 
- Flexible work environment- Hybrid Model (3 days a week from the office, 2 days from home)

EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT & SCAM DISCLAIMER

  • EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT- Farfetch is an equal opportunities employer ensuring that all applicants are treated equally and fairly throughout our recruitment process. We are determined that no applicant experiences discrimination on the basis of sex, race, ethnicity, religion or belief, disability, age, gender identity, ancestry, sexual orientation, veteran status, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, or any other basis prohibited by applicable law. 

  • SCAM DISCLAIMER- It has come to our attention that there may be fraudulent activities involving individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent Farfetch in order to attract candidates to a SCAM. Please be aware that Farfetch does not conduct recruitment processes through messaging apps or any unofficial communication channels, other than our official careers website. Additionally, Farfetch will never ask candidates for any form of payment during the recruitment process.

raw.title: Senior Financial Analyst
raw.description:
Farfetch is a leading global marketplace for the luxury fashion industry. The Farfetch Marketplace connects customers in over 190 countries and territories with items from more than 50 countries and over 1,400 of the world’s best brands, boutiques, and department stores, delivering a truly unique shopping experience and access to the most extensive selection of luxury on a global marketplace. 

FINANCE 

We're a diverse team who partners and supports the business to enable delivery against our strategic and financial goals. All of our functions have an instrumental role within Farfetch to drive forward a financially sustainable business, ensuring we set the guardrails for financial control and enable financial performance.

 

LONDON

Our London office is located in Old Street, London’s tech hub, and is home to a wide range of teams. Our open space is ideal for collaborative work and sharing ideas. We also have a large outdoor terrace, which is the perfect spot to have a team lunch or host events. 

ROLE

As a Senior Financial Analyst you will partner directly with functional senior leaders helping to create a world-class business partnering function who are pivotal in turning insights into actions, driving business performance, and profitability, and championing the long-term financial health of the FARFETCH Group. This role will ensure that the organization operates with financial coherence and that the senior leaders and stakeholders have a transparent view of how their areas of responsibility are performing, giving clarity on the financial impact of their strategic, operational, and trading decisions.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Act as a trusted advisor, partnering with cross-functional teams to understand their business objectives and provide financial guidance

  • Identify opportunities for cost optimization, process improvements, and revenue growth initiatives

  • Help to bring alignment of financial management across the diverse elements of the organization, standardizing reporting and bringing focus to key financial KPIs

  • Deliver analysis, insight, and recommendations on the financial implications of key business decisions in a timely and efficient way

  • Challenge the organisation to deliver financial goals aligned with the Group's operating and financial strategy through business partnering, driving growth in top-line revenue and efficiencies in the cost base and working capital

  • Delivery of financial planning, budgeting, and forecasting for functional areas, translating the vision of the business into a long-term financial strategy, and supporting the development of the strategy to drive the business

  • Identify and implement process improvements and participate in existing reporting enhancements with the mindset of continuous improvement

WHO YOU ARE

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA/ACCA/ACA is a plus

  • Proven experience in P&L ownership and financial planning, within retail, technology, or the e-Commerce industry is advantageous

  • Proven people leadership and management experience, able to lead with an authentic style and ensure team delivery to high standards

  • Strong commercial acumen, with an ability to influence strategic business decisions, keeping the financial health of the business front of mind

  • A strategic mindset, with an ability to have a long-term vision with an eye on detail

  • Self-motivated in a fast-paced and rapidly changing environment with competing deadlines, driven to deliver results

  • A strong team player with the ability to interact and effectively communicate with those outside of Finance teams to deliver preferred outcomes

REWARDS & BENEFITS

  • Flexible working environment and well-being support and tools 

  • Extra days off, sabbatical program and days for you to give back for the community 

  • Training opportunities and free access to Udemy 

  • Flexible benefits program

EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT

  • FARFETCH is committed to being an inclusive workplace where diversity in all its forms is celebrated. We make employment decisions without regard to race, religious creed, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, ancestry, marital status, medical condition as defined by state law, physical or mental disability, military service or veteran status, pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, genetic information or any other classification protected by applicable federal, state or local laws or ordinances. If you require special accommodation, please let us know.

LONDON

ROLE

The Legal Team at Farfetch is seeking a Senior Legal Counsel - Regulatory for a broad regulatory and commercial role. This is a unique opportunity to advise on regulatory matters within a global, fast-moving and innovative business. You will enjoy a diverse role, delivering high-quality strategic legal advice across multiple operational territories in conjunction with our wider international Legal Team. You will work closely with the broader legal team and all business areas.

Acting as a true business partner, this role requires someone who is commercially minded, intellectually curious and hands-on, able to quickly understand and apply new sets of international laws and regulations - identifying and mitigating risks, as well as seizing opportunities. It is a role for someone with strong professional ethics and the energy, interest and experience to pursue a large array of regulatory and commercial matters. 


WHAT YOU'LL DO
  • Advise on payment regulation and broader regulatory frameworks, including in relation to digital regulation, product compliance and consumer protection
  • Track and assess existing and new requirements for the Farfetch Group, with a focus on payments regulation, as well as advise on their implementation
  • Identify, monitor and evaluate relevant regulatory risks and enforcement trends, and take proactive steps to mitigate these
  • Develop strategies for, and engage with, relevant regulators 
  • Advise on commercial matters, including on contractual agreements with partners and payment processors, and ensure a compliant payment model
  • Work on tariffs-related matters and advise from a legal perspective
  • Negotiate, draft and review commercial contracts, policies, guidance and other legal documentation 
  • Provide proactive, strategic and pragmatic advice
  • Liaise with external law firms, where external support is needed
  • Support the Group Legal VP, Regulatory Legal Team and the business in ensuring it operates in a compliant manner
  • Use legal technology and AI tools in an ethical way to deliver advice efficiently, and help the team adopt and get the best from these tools

    • WHO YOU ARE
  • A qualified lawyer with at least 4 years’ PQE and superior analytical skills and creative problem-solving skills. Prior in-house experience would be beneficial 
  • Have excellent training, preferably in a top-tier law firm
  • Have experience advising on payments regulation and commercial matters
  • Have proven ability to assess new pieces of international legislation/regulation and apply them on a risk-based basis to a business 
  • Have the curiosity and ability to absorb a lot of information quickly, apply it in assessments, and drive implementation
  • Be able to understand nuances and complexities, and translate these into commercial, pragmatic, and concise advice in the context of a global business
  • Have a strong work ethic and attention to detail, be highly proactive, organized and efficient, able to work on fast-moving projects
  • Be able to work autonomously but also well in teams, supervising legal counsel and supporting the Group Legal VP and Regulatory Legal Team
  • Possess excellent communication, organization and drafting skills
  • Driven, forward-thinking, robust, innovative and agile, with commercial acumen

raw.description:
We’re building the next generation of employee benefits infrastructure.

At Happl, we help global teams design, manage, and scale benefits that actually work for their people by using AI, across flex allowances, benefits, insurance, recognition, and wellbeing, all in one intelligent platform.

Happl is backed by leading investors such as YCombinator, 6Degrees Capital, Haatch, Portage, and more, known for backing leading companies such as Deel, Rippling, Airbnb, Coinbase, Dropbox, and most recently was awarded a place in the UK’s top 100 startups for 2026.

About the role

As Financial Controller at Happl, you’ll own the financial engine of the business — everything from the cash in the bank to the numbers our board and investors use to make decisions runs through you. You’ll run the monthly close, the full revenue cycle, the compliance calendar across two jurisdictions, and our treasury position, and you’ll decide how all of it gets built, systemised, and automated.

This is a hands-on, high-autonomy role with a direct line to leadership. You won’t be managing a process someone else designed — you’ll be deciding what good looks like across revenue, cash, compliance, and reporting, then making it happen. You’ll work closely with the CEO, the board, our investors, and our outsourced bookkeeping, audit, and tax partners, holding all of it to a standard that matches the product we’ve built.

We’re FCA-regulated and YCombinator-backed, having raised $11m to date, and we give global employers a single place to design, deliver, and manage benefits across 160+ countries and 70+ languages — which means the finance function behind the product has to be just as sharp as the product itself. We’re entering our next phase of growth, with an ambitious revenue trajectory and an expanding international footprint, and this role sits at the centre of it.

What you’ll be doing

  • Owning the monthly close on a fixed timetable — management accounts, balance sheet integrity, accruals, prepayments, and the revenue and cost reconciliations that sit behind them

  • Writing the commentary that explains what’s actually happened in the business, not just what the numbers say

  • Producing the monthly investor reporting pack and the financial sections of board materials — ARR and revenue analysis, cash and runway, burn efficiency, unit economics, cohort and retention metrics, and budget versus actual

  • Owning the full revenue cycle — invoicing, collections, aged debt, and revenue recognition across a multi-currency, multi-contract subscription base

  • Leading the rollout of automated billing and revenue recognition tooling, moving us from manual tracking to a system that scales without adding headcount

  • Managing our two legal entities — a US TopCo and a UK operating company — including statutory accounts, audit preparation, intercompany accounting, transfer pricing mechanics, and FX exposure between them

  • Owning the compliance calendar end to end across both jurisdictions — UK VAT returns, corporation tax, US federal and state filings, sales tax where applicable, and payroll taxes

  • Supporting our FCA regulatory reporting obligations and the financial controls that sit behind them

  • Running monthly payroll across jurisdictions, pension and benefits administration, employee expenses, and the finance side of onboarding and offboarding

  • Owning the cash position and treasury strategy — cash flow forecasting, working capital, FX management, and structuring how we hold company funds to earn a sensible return without taking risk we shouldn’t

  • Managing our outsourced bookkeeping, accounting, and tax partners — holding them to deadlines and quality, and pulling work in-house where doing so makes us faster

  • Owning the finance tech stack and having a strong opinion on it, actively replacing manual work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across reconciliations, invoice processing, variance analysis, and reporting drafts

  • Leveraging AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT to speed up your own work and build the systems that let finance scale without adding headcount

  • Acting as the financial conscience of the business, with a direct line to the founders and a real say in how we grow

What we’re looking for

  • Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA), or qualified by experience with a track record that stands up to scrutiny

  • Genuine ownership of a monthly close cycle and management reporting pack, start to finish

  • Strong technical grounding in revenue recognition, accruals accounting, and balance sheet control

  • Comfortable with tax and compliance across VAT, corporation tax, and payroll, ideally spanning both the UK and US

  • AI-native in your approach — you already use AI tools in your day-to-day work and can talk specifically about what you’ve automated and what it saved you

  • Exceptional attention to detail, alongside the judgement to know when precision matters and when speed does

  • A clear communicator — you can explain a number to a non-finance audience without patronising them or losing them

  • Ideally, SaaS or subscription business experience, particularly ARR reporting and deferred revenue, and familiarity with modern billing infrastructure like Xero or Stripe

  • Comfort with SQL, Python, or low-code automation tools is a bonus, not a requirement, but it will make your life here significantly easier

What to expect

Being Financial Controller at Happl is not a maintenance role. You’ll be building the finance function as you run it — choosing the systems, designing the controls, and deciding how billing, revenue recognition, and reporting should work as we scale into new markets and currencies. That’s not a caveat; it’s the role.

Some weeks will be genuinely rewarding — a reporting pack you built gives the board real clarity, a manual process you automated saves the team hours every month, a treasury decision you made puts real value on the table. Some will be hard — closing the books on a fixed timetable, holding partners and advisors to a deadline, and making judgement calls across two jurisdictions with incomplete information.

What you get in return is real scope. You’ll own the whole picture — revenue, cash, compliance, treasury, and reporting — across two jurisdictions and 160+ countries of operations, with a direct line to the founders and reporting that goes straight to the board and our investors. This is the foundation of a finance function that will grow with the business, and the right person grows with it.

Why join Happl

  • Be part of building something that genuinely matters — the future of how companies support their people

  • Competitive salary that reflects the impact you’ll have

  • Real equity — a meaningful stake in what we’re building together

  • Hybrid working from day one, with the trust and flexibility to do your best work

  • Your own Happl account — use the platform you’re helping to build and shape

  • Private Health Insurance, because we genuinely care about how you’re doing

  • Dental insurance, including family cover

  • A personal Wellbeing budget to spend however wellbeing works for you — no questions asked

  • A dedicated L&D budget to grow in the direction that excites you

  • Pension — we’re invested in your future, not just the short term

About the Interview

  • Stage 1: 20-min Intro call with Ben Shorrock (Head of Operations)

  • Stage 2: Short task

  • Stage 3: 30-min deep dive and task review with Ben T (CEO) & Ben S (Ops)

Additional Details

  • Location: London, Holborn

  • Team: Finance

  • Reports to: CEO

  • Working arrangement: Hybrid (4+ Days in Office)

raw.description:
The Account Manager (AM) is a key client partner and collaborative leader within Infinite Lambda. Responsible for owning and growing accounts, AMs play a crucial role in ensuring successful delivery, maintaining client satisfaction, and driving commercial outcomes. While AMs are expected to operate independently, they collaborate closely with delivery teams and seek support from Senior Account Managers when needed.

This role belongs to the Account Management Department, part of the broader Customer Success Division. AMs work cross-functionally with Engineering Excellence and Delivery Excellence teams, ensuring alignment between client goals and internal execution.

This role does not include direct reports but requires strong leadership through influence. You will collaborate with engineers, architects, analysts, project managers, and commercial teams to deliver measurable client outcomes and drive revenue growth.

Key Objectives

  • Drive sustainable, forecastable growth: Secure new business opportunities from assigned accounts, retain clients, and ensure their satisfaction through exceptional delivery.

  • Build enduring partnerships: Establish yourself as a trusted partner to clients, ensuring long-term collaboration and profitability.

You lead by example and foster a culture based on trust, empowerment, and excellence with your accounts and the teams you work with.

 

Detailed Responsibilities

Client Relationship Management

  • Develop and nurture strong relationships with assigned clients, serving as the main point of contact and advocate for their needs;

  • Understand each client’s business objectives, challenges, and strategic goals to deliver tailored solutions that align with their vision;

  • Proactively establish Infinite Lambda as a trusted partner, consistently delivering tangible value and maintain client engagement ;

  • Facilitate regular check-ins, quarterly business reviews, and strategic planning sessions to ensure alignment and promote long-term partnerships.

  • Act as a cultural ambassador, fostering trust-based relationships that reflect Infinite Lambda’s values and create a positive, lasting experience for both clients and colleagues;

  • Champion sustainable growth by aligning client success with long-term partnership and responsible use of data and AI technology.

Revenue Growth & Account Development

  • Identify upselling and cross-selling opportunities within client environments;

  • Drive renewals and contract discussions, with support from commercial leadership as needed;

  • Drive financial performance by meeting revenue targets, securing competitive pricing, and maintaining consistent growth in gross margins and profitability;

  • Proactively manage opportunity pipelines, converting opportunities into measurable revenue.

Strategic Account Planning

  • Define and implement account strategies in line with the direction provided by the Chief Customer Success Officer (CCO);

  • Collaborate with sales, marketing, and delivery teams to develop comprehensive account strategies that leverage Infinite Lambda’s offerings and expertise;

  • Analyse client industries, competitors, and market trends to identify growth opportunities and mitigate risks;

  • Contribute insights to product and service development based on client feedback and market needs.

 

Sales Handover & Onboarding

  • Take ownership of new accounts after contract signature;

  • Lead smooth client onboarding processes in coordination with delivery and sales.

 

Collaboration & Internal Alignment

raw.title: Senior Publisher Partnerships Manager – Enterprise Gaming
raw.description:
InMobi (Corporate)

InMobi Group is a global technology company shaping the future of agentic commerce and advertising. Through its ecosystem of businesses — including InMobi Advertising and flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi leverages data, machine learning, and generative AI to help brands reach audiences more precisely and consumers discover products more intuitively. Glance, which is pioneering new models of agentic commerce, is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd.

InMobi Advertising

InMobi Advertising, part of global technology company InMobi, is an agentic advertising platform helping brands and merchants achieve their business outcomes. Through its proprietary intelligence, AI-led solutions, and vast consumer reach — including flagship consumer platform Glance — InMobi Advertising delivers the omnichannel performance defining what's next in advertising and commerce. Glance is owned and operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of InMobi Pte. Ltd. To learn more, visit advertising.inmobi.com.

Glance

Glance is an intelligent shopping agent, redefining the commerce experience. Powered by proprietary agentic intelligence and generative AI, Glance delivers a hyper-personalized consumer experience across mobile and TV — shaping the new era of shopping. Glance is operated by Glance InMobi Pte. Ltd., a non-consolidated subsidiary of global technology leader InMobi, and is backed by Mithril Capital, Google and Jio Platforms. To learn more, visit glance.com.

Overview of the Role:

The Enterprise Gaming Partnerships team is part of InMobi's Supply organization and drives strategic growth across our advertising exchange. The team manages direct relationships with the world's leading mobile game developers and app publishers. It helps them get the most from their ad monetization through in-app bidding, mediation integrations, and high-quality global demand.

The role is based in London and is externally-facing. You'll build and grow partnerships with top-tier gaming and app publishers, with a focus on in-app formats such as rewarded video, interstitial, banner, and native. You'll also help publishers grow their user base by connecting them to InMobi's user acquisition (UA) solutions. Internally, you'll be the link between the publisher ecosystem and InMobi's Product, Demand, Marketplace, and Ad Quality teams, keeping everyone aligned so that partners get results.

Reporting to the Director of Enterprise Gaming, you'll own a book of business across EMEA, shape growth strategy for each partner, and represent InMobi at the major gaming and app industry events. You'll play a central part in strengthening InMobi's position as a leading monetization partner for gaming and apps.

The Impact You'll Make:

  • Represent and manage a portfolio of high-priority gaming and app publishers. Find growth opportunities, manage risks, and build plans that run across several quarters.
  • Take ownership of a defined book of strategic publisher accounts within your first 90 days.
  • Build strong relationships with studios. Learn their monetization stack, game economies, ad formats, and retention goals well enough to spot new opportunities and act on them.
  • Meet or exceed revenue targets every quarter while giving partners an outstanding experience.
  • Grow share of wallet within partners' mediation setups (AppLovin MAX, Google AdMob/Open Bidding, and Unity LevelPlay). Do this through bidding integrations, new placements, format expansion, and better performance.
  • Track key health metrics such as fill rate, eCPM, revenue per daily active user (ARPDAU), ad quality, and margin. Diagnose problems and work with internal teams to fix them.
  • Find cross-sell opportunities: help publishers grow their player base through InMobi's UA offering, and open brand demand for their inventory.
  • Work with Product, Demand, and Marketplace teams to line up supply and demand strategies, including new ad products and direct deals for gaming inventory.
  • Run enablement between publisher partners and internal Sales teams, so that buyers understand the value of gaming audiences and partners adopt new features.
  • Attend key industry events such as Pocket Gamer Connects, Gamesforum, MAU, GDC and Gamescom, and represent InMobi credibly in the gaming ecosystem.
  • Deepen your working technical knowledge of SDK integration, in-app bidding, mediation waterfalls, and how an SSP works.
  • Coach peers to raise the team's capabilities and contribute to the wider team's success.
  • Build growth plans with Business Development, Marketplace, Product, and Engineering, using publisher feedback to shape goals and the product roadmap.

The Experience We Need:

  • A flexible, startup mindset, a strong sense of ownership, and a track record of success in fast-paced, high-growth environments.
  • A proven ability to build, grow, and sell into customer relationships, ideally with existing accounts at mobile gaming or app companies.
  • Success in building account growth plans, influencing decision-makers, and agreeing on shared goals.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. You can draw insight from monetization data, A/B tests, and performance dashboards, and you work well with ambiguity.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities with solid process and project management.
  • Proactive and action-oriented, and comfortable working across functions and time zones.
  • An established network across the EMEA mobile gaming ecosystem, including hubs such as London, Paris, Istanbul, Helsinki, Barcelona, Berlin, and Tel Aviv, and the confidence to meet partners in person at industry events.
  • Hands-on knowledge of in-app monetization: mediation platforms, in-app bidding, ad networks, and SSPs. Experience with UA or performance marketing is a plus.
  • Readiness to learn new systems and keep up with market trends such as privacy changes and mediation dynamics.
  • A collaborative team player with strong interpersonal skills, leadership instincts, and a sense of humor.

At InMobi, you'll be surrounded by people who…

  • Think big and act fast: We're entrepreneurial, thrive in ambiguity, and love solving high-impact problems
  • Are passionate, fanatically driven, and take immense pride in their work: We care deeply about the impact we create and continuously push our potential
  • Own their outcomes: We take responsibility, make bold decisions, and execute with confidence
  • Embrace freedom with accountability: We value autonomy and understand that trust comes with responsibility
  • Believe in lifelong learning: We welcome feedback, challenge ourselves to grow, and aren't afraid to take smart risks

Award-winning culture, best-in-class benefits

Our compensation philosophy enables us to provide a competitive salary that drives high performance while balancing business needs and pay parity. We determine compensation based on a wide variety of factors, including role, nature of experience, skills, and location.

For this role, an InMobian may also receive variable pay in the form of an annual variable bonus or quarterly variable bonus/sales incentive, as deemed per policy, in addition to fixed compensation.

In addition to cash compensation, based on the position, an InMobian can receive equity in the form of ESOPs (Employee Stock Option Plan). We believe that our employees/personnel should have the ability to own a part of the entity they are a part of. Therefore, the entity employing you may elect to provide such stock to you. Ownership of stock enables us to treat our employer company as our own and base our decisions on the company's best interests. To encourage a spirit of shared ownership, we grant InMobians relevant company stock(s). As you contribute to the growth of your company, certain stocks may be issued to you in recognition of your contribution.

If this sounds like the kind of team, role, values, benefits, and challenges that excite you, we'd love to hear from you!

InMobi is an equal opportunity employer
InMobi is a place where everyone can grow. Howsoever you identify, and whatever background you bring with you, we invite you to apply if this sounds like a role that would make you excited to work.

InMobi provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

The InMobi Culture

At InMobi, culture isn't a buzzword; it's an ethos woven by every InMobian, reflecting our diverse backgrounds and experiences.

We thrive on challenges and seize every opportunity for growth. Our core values — thinking big, being passionate, showing accountability, and taking ownership with freedom — guide us in every decision we make.

We believe in nurturing and investing in your development through continuous learning and career progression with our InMobi Live Your Potential program.

InMobi is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the hiring process and in the workplace.

Visit https://www.inmobi.com/company/careers to better understand our benefits, values, and more!

offer.title: Data Scientist - iwocaPay Credit Risk Modelling

raw.title: Data Scientist - iwocaPay Credit Risk Modelling
raw.description:
Data Scientist - iwocaPay Credit Risk Modelling

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom (one day per week in office requirement)

We're looking for a Data Scientist to join the iwocaPay Risk Squad.

You'll own credit models that decide who iwocaPay can safely fund, on what terms, and how far the product can grow. You'll help shape how risk modelling develops.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We've already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Risk Squad owns credit risk and fraud for iwocaPay, iwoca's Buy Now Pay Later product for businesses. The aim is to lend to every business likely to repay, and to spot the ones that aren't.

The squad works across three areas:

  • Lending decisions. Building and improving the automated credit model.

  • The portfolio. Tracking losses, chargebacks, and seller performance, and deciding which segments to grow or pull back from.

  • New products. Designing the risk side of each one before it launches.

The squad is small and new – two data scientists, a risk analyst and a risk lead.

The role

As a Data Scientist in the Risk Squad, you'll co-own every credit model with the other data scientist and review one another's work. The job is mostly supervised ML on tabular data, with a fair amount of data engineering as the squad moves onto its own pipelines. You'll start on the automated credit model and take on the invoice financing models over time. You can also test ideas with iwoca's other lending data science teams, who work on similar credit problems.

You'll choose what to work on and write the plans you deliver. Much of the squad's work happens in iwocaPay's product and strategy meetings, so your models shape the roadmap. You'll also help set up how the squad works – what it monitors, and the guidelines it follows.

Live project examples:

  • Model architecture. Rethinking the model around how iwocaPay actually lends: overlapping facilities, short terms, and a growing set of products a customer can use.

  • Blending datasets. Bringing more iwocaPay-specific data into the models while still drawing on iwoca's larger core lending dataset, through methods such as transfer learning.

  • Invoice financing. Building a credit risk model from scratch for a new product on a segment iwoca hasn’t lent to before. Plus finding the modelling opportunities elsewhere in the funnel, like in our offers...

The requirements

Essential:

  • Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field – typically a degree or Master's in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, or similar. You reason about uncertainty and calibration as first-order concerns.

  • Production ML. You have built supervised ML models on tabular data end to end – exploration, training, deployment, and monitoring.

  • Ownership. You work well in a small, early-stage team where priorities move quickly. You build what you need as you go, and take loosely defined problems from framing to a landed decision.

  • Judgement. You know when a model is good enough to go live, and when it needs more work. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right.

  • AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – a modelling pipeline, a prototype, or a tool others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail for non-technical colleagues in product, risk, and leadership.

Bonus:

  • Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk modelling or lending.

  • Non-linear methods. You have used gradient boosting or neural networks on tabular data in production.

  • Combining datasets. You have used transfer learning, domain adaptation, or similar methods on data sources of different size and relevance.

  • Data engineering. You have built data pipelines and managed datasets alongside your modelling work.

  • Coding. You can write code for analysis. The squad works in Python.

The salary

We expect to pay from £60,000 to £80,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

  • iwoca benefits & policies

  • Interview welcome pack

Compensation: £60K – £90K

raw.title: Growth Associate - M&A Platform
raw.description:
You’re joining manda, iwoca’s M&A platform, at a pivotal moment. After early success working with existing iwoca customers, we’re now turning to the open market to help more business owners exit.

That’s why we’re looking for a Growth Associate to join the team. This is a 6-month fixed-term role for someone smart, hungry and entrepreneurial. With the right traction the role will convert into a permanent role at the forefront of manda’s growth efforts.

The company

Selling a small business is hard. Only one in five UK SME owners has a formal exit plan, yet half are counting on their business to fund their retirement. Below £10m in enterprise value, most M&A advisers can't make the economics work, so a generation of owner-managers is getting ready to step back with no realistic route to a sale.

manda exists to fix that. We match owners with serious buyers, from search funds to private equity, and handle the whole process in one place, including financial due diligence and acquisition finance. Our first sale is done, and we're now opening manda up beyond iwoca's own customers.

manda is part of iwoca, one of Europe's leading fintech lenders, which has provided more than £4 billion in funding to over 150,000 businesses since 2012. That gives us what a traditional adviser doesn't have: a deep footprint in the SME economy, a lender's data and infrastructure, and deals run on clean, automated processes rather than spreadsheets.

The team

You'll report to manda's Venture Lead and work day to day with our Transaction Managers, the dealmakers who run each sale, and our Partnerships Manager, who builds our referral network with accountants, solicitors and wealth managers. You'll also work with iwoca's marketing & sales team and have access to their tools and know-how.

The role

Your mission is to grow the number of businesses manda takes to market, by finding owners who are serious about selling and bringing them into a first meeting with one of our Transaction Managers.

With an ethos of smarter, not louder, you’ll build on iwoca’s existing models to work out which owners are getting ready to sell and which businesses will attract a buyer, then reach them personally by email, LinkedIn and phone. We'd rather approach the right few hundred owners well than the wrong ten thousand badly.

  • Decide who we contact. Own the target lists and the logic behind them, and keep sharpening them on what actually predicts a seller and a strong business.

  • Convert interest. Write and send the outreach yourself, follow up with owners who respond, and book them in with a Transaction Manager.

  • Find what works. Run several experiments at once, back what produces meetings and drop what doesn't. Letters, events and ideas of your own can all earn a place.

  • Make manda credible. Owners look us up before they reply. Help make sure what they find, from our website to LinkedIn, gives them a reason to get in touch.

Who you are

You don't need to be a marketer or have years of experience. You need to be smart, resourceful and quick to learn from what isn't working, and to want ownership of something real.

  • You're entrepreneurial. You've started, sold or built something, even if it was small, and you don't wait for a plan before getting going.

  • You write well. Your messages are short, clear and human, the kind a busy owner actually answers, and you're just as at ease on the phone with someone who has spent thirty years building their business.

  • You follow through. A reply that never becomes a meeting is a lead lost.

  • You're honest about results. You'd rather report a bad week than dress it up.

  • You're AI-savvy. You use AI to research, personalise and write at a scale one person couldn't otherwise reach, and you automate whatever you find yourself doing twice.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Some experience in outreach, sales or growth, whether in an SDR or BDR role, marketing, a startup or a project of your own. Evidence of initiative matters more than a polished CV.

  • Numerate and analytical. Working out who to contact is as much of this job as contacting them.

  • Comfortable with rejection. Most owners won't reply, and plenty who do won't be ready yet.

  • A genuine interest in SMEs, M&A or how businesses change hands.

  • Based in London and available full-time.

Bonus:

  • Hands-on with outbound tools such as HubSpot or LinkedIn Sales Navigator.

raw.title: BDR Manager
raw.description:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $14M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY.

The Role

  • We have strong product market fit. In 2025 we grew ~5x with world class net dollar retention, mostly from founder-led sales, and now have AEs hitting quota with an emerging playbook.

  • We're looking for another BDR Manager to accelerate our outbound engine as we scale in 2026. You'll own a team of ~10 BDRs and be responsible for the pipeline that fuels our growth.

  • You will report to Dave Bentham (Head of Sales) and work closely with our AEs, marketing, and leadership team to make sure the top of funnel is consistently feeding high-quality pipeline.

What You’ll Be Doing

Set the strategy

  • Work with Dave and the rest of leadership to define ICP, targeting, and outbound messaging.

  • Translate company targets into clear, measurable BDR goals and ensure pipeline expectations are distributed strategically across the team.

  • Continuously iterate on outbound plays, channels, and sequences to improve conversion at every stage.

  • Develop the BDR team to be a talent pool for the rest of the organisation through a culture of constant learning

Set your team

  • Manage and develop a team of ~10 BDRs across inbound and outbound.

  • Work alongside our recruiters to grow the team as we scale.

  • Be accountable for team performance. Coach underperformers, promote top performers, and set a high bar across the board.

  • Our BDR team is the talent engine for the entire GTM team. Nurturing the best people and helping them be ready for the next role is crucial.

Set the operating cadence

  • Define qualification criteria and handoff processes that set AEs up to close.

  • Build repeatable outbound plays that convert, and partner with marketing where needed.

  • Establish pipeline generation rigor: activity metrics, and predictable output.

  • Run weekly team reviews, call coaching sessions, and continuous improvement loops.

What You Bring:

  • 4+ years in business development and/or outbound sales, with at least some time managing a BDR or SDR team.

  • Experience scaling a BDR team (e.g. growing from a handful of reps to 10+) or managing a team of that size.

  • Strong instincts for messaging, targeting, and what makes outbound actually work.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity: you can build process, playbooks, and territory strategy.

  • Bonus: the deeper your knowledge of RevOps, data, and GTM tools the better.

⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

  • Need lots of structure or polished specs.

  • You like spending weeks agonizing on a single initiative, or don’t want to rapidly iterate and run experiments.

  • Require detailed instructions.

❌ This role is definitely not for you if you:

  • Prefer remote or hybrid work (requires 4+ days in London office) and/or can’t travel to clients (US+Europe)

  • Don’t enjoy the pace of an early-stage startup.

  • Want to carry your own deals instead of building and coaching a team.

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you the ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

  • 💰 Salary: £80-120k OTE + equity

  • 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays

  • 🥕 £450 Monthly Office Dinner Allowance

  • ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere

  • 🍼 Generous parental leave policy

  • 💼 Pension plan

  • 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office

  • 🎉 Team events and dinners

  • 🚀 Work directly with the founders to scale the systems that power enterprise AI

  • 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace

🎫 Visas & Relocation

We can sponsor visas or offer relocation for exceptional candidates.

Interview Process

Stage 1 – Intro call with Talent Acquisition, Seray (40min).

Stage 2 – Hiring Manager interview with Head of Sales, Dave (60min).

Stage 3 – Coffee chat with peer, Jack (30min)

Stage 4 – Case study and time on site with Dave & team (1hour).

Final Stage – Founders interview with CEO, Anders (45min).

If there is mutual fit, we move to references and offer.

raw.description:
LiveRamp is shaping the future of responsible data collaboration between the world’s leading brands, retailers, financial services providers, and healthcare innovators. As consumers embrace new AI-driven experiences, the LiveRamp data collaboration network exponentially expands the breadth and accuracy of the data on which marketing AI capabilities operate, powering deeper customer insight and measurable performance on a global scale. LiveRamp is headquartered in San Francisco, California, with offices worldwide. Learn more at LiveRamp.com.

We are looking for a highly-motivated, business-minded Legal and Data Ethics Operations Analyst. This person will help the Data Ethics and Legal teams solve internal problems, implement goal-oriented strategies and play a key role in the Data Ethics team.

This role strengthens operational execution across jurisdictions through process improvement, responsible AI enablement, privacy and legal operations, playbook development, and effective management of data subject requests.

You will:

  • Coordinate data subject request management, including intake, categorization, routing, deadline tracking, documentation, communications, and closure; work with the Data Ethics team on high-risk, complex, sensitive, or multi-jurisdictional requests.

  • Build and maintain practical playbooks, decision trees, checklists, templates, escalation criteria, and role-based guidance for recurring data ethics, privacy, legal, and regulatory processes.

  • Manage privacy questionnaire workflows by coordinating intake, preparing AI-assisted first drafts from approved information, maintaining supporting evidence, and escalating questions requiring legal, privacy, security, or data ethics judgment.

  • Support the design of responsible AI controls including approved-source use, permissions, confidentiality, traceability, version control, audit trails, quality checks, and human approval before material outputs are used.

  • Study our organizational workflows and processes to recommend and implement changes to help improve business processes and optimize overall operations.

  • Participate in creating team functional process documentation, creating presentation materials and facilitating or leading cross functional teams through projects and/or issues.

  • Co-ordinate, write and maintain information and knowledge resources to ensure it is kept up to date and supports users of the system(s). This includes managing and organizing documents within the Data Ethics department to ensure that they are accurate, up-to-date, and easily accessible.

  • Create, modify, and manage content on the Data Ethics intranet site.

  • Assist with the project planning, scheduling, and documentation of various department projects, such as working with subject matter experts to assist with designing and organizing training course content and may use instructional technology tools to develop participant materials, videos, practical exercises, and interactive eLearning.

  • Prepare operational reporting on questionnaire and request volumes, turnaround times, escalations, recurring issues, automation performance, risks, and improvement opportunities.

Your team will:

Our Data Ethics operations program is designed to enable LiveRamp to meet its privacy-related legal requirements and reasonable expectations of clients while minimizing and mitigating risk to LiveRamp. Our mission is to help the business find safe and legal ways to use data for the betterment of our products, services and consumers. The team operates as a connected, cross-border function that helps LiveRamp find safe, legal, ethical, and scalable ways to use data while supporting consistent execution across all locations.

About you:

  • Degree in a relevant discipline

  • Experience in a similar role required with relevant experience in data privacy, data ethics, legal operations, regulatory operations, or related process enablement

  • Experience completing critical analysis, review and editing of written documents

  • Ability to work in a collaborative manner to develop strong working relationships with the business and key stakeholders to facilitate data compliance while enabling commercial opportunities and support them in improving data protection and governance practices

  • Comfortable receiving loose requirements and working with internal team members to identify project objectives, collaborate to further define requirements, pull and validate the data, present the data to the end-users, and make refinements as needed. Strong communication and organizational skills are a must.

  • Ability to translate complex legal, regulatory, and data ethics requirements into practical processes, playbooks, decision trees, and guidance.

  • Experience applying AI or automation to privacy questionnaires, document or contract-template updates, knowledge retrieval, playbook creation, triage, or workflow orchestration.

  • Hands-on experience building, configuring, or implementing AI agents, automation, or AI-assisted workflows in a controlled business environment.

  • Self-motivated, proactive, and eager to dive into the business, data workflows, and technology

  • Comfort with ambiguity, multi-tasking, and independence

  • Excellent written/verbal communication, presentation, drafting and negotiation skills

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

  • Ability to organize, prioritize, manage deadlines, and handle complex escalations in a fast-paced and demanding work environment

  • Comfortable expressing a point of view and influencing change, as appropriate

  • Strong proficiency in Salesforce and Google Suite applications, especially Google Slides (preferred)

We use automated decision systems (ADS) as part of our recruitment and hiring process. If you require an accommodation or believe that the use of an ADS may create a barrier to your application or participation in the hiring process due to a disability or other protected characteristic, please let us know. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations and ensuring an equitable hiring experience for all candidates.

To all recruitment agencies: LiveRamp does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, LiveRamp employees or any other company location. LiveRamp is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Drive the technical strategy, architecture, and roadmap for the Identity Engine team, ensuring alignment with LiveRamp's overall engineering and product goals.

Anticipate and resolve complex issues and conflicts that extend beyond the team's direct area of responsibility.
Hold other teams accountable for quality and timely delivery when dependencies exist.
Actively engage in long-term (12-month) Product planning and priority setting, helping to define the strategic roadmap for Identity Engine.
Be the primary technical liaison for Product Management, ensuring technical feasibility and strategic alignment of product initiatives.
Help identify, develop, and hire strategic skills to enhance the overall capabilities of the LiveRamp engineering organization.
Maintain a significant individual contributor (IC) component (approximately 50% of time), focusing on complex technical challenges, architecture, and code quality reviews.

2+ years of demonstrating strong leadership skills, with a proven ability to deliver on products as the technical lead.
8+ years of hands-on development experience, ideally leveraging Java or other JVM based languages.
You oversee coding of critical areas and develop the most difficult code across multiple system components, driving high coding standards and improving development practices.
Demonstrated experience driving complex designs, high-quality interface/API designs, and overall architecture improvements across multiple teams and services, leading design reviews and ensuring consistent architecture.
Track record of driving product/service design and vision inside engineering, using global industry and market trends to deliver successful products and fulfilling unexpressed client wants.
Experience mentoring more junior engineers, providing technical guidance, and contributing to talent identification at Staff Level & above.
Strong communicator. Sharing information regularly and concisely.

Knowledge of the adTech space and particularly the identifiers used in the field.

raw.title: Staff AI Deployment Strategist - UK & Nordics
raw.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

 

As Staff AI Deployment Strategist, you will shape how some of the most ambitious enterprises in the UK & Nordics region adopt frontier AI at scale.

This is a senior, high-impact role at the intersection of strategy, technology, and execution. You will work directly on Mistral’s most strategic opportunities and largest deliveries, helping customers move from ambition to measurable business outcomes. You will frame complex AI transformation programs, turn executive priorities into actionable roadmaps, and ensure that Mistral delivers systems that are valuable, scalable, and trusted.

You will also act as a senior sponsor on our most critical customer programs, bringing judgment, structure, and delivery excellence to high-stakes engagements. Your mandate is to raise the ambition and quality of AI adoption: helping customers identify where AI can create step-change value, making the right trade-offs, and ensuring that execution matches the strategic promise.

This role is ideal for an experienced strategy consultant, transformation leader, or senior operator who wants to move from advising on change to building it directly with frontier AI technology.

 

What You Will Do

  • Shape high-impact AI transformations

    • Partner closely with Mistral’s Sales leadership in the UK & Nordics to qualify opportunities, align on account strategy, and drive executive engagement.

    • Work with senior customer stakeholders to identify where frontier AI can create material business value.

    • Structure complex opportunities into clear, credible, and executable transformation programs.

    • Translate strategic ambition into delivery roadmaps, success metrics, and operating plans.

    • Help customers make the right trade-offs between ambition, feasibility, speed, and long-term scalability.

  • Sponsor Mistral’s most strategic deliveries

    • Act as a senior sponsor on the largest and most complex customer programs, primarily in the UK & Nordics and potentially cross-region as priorities evolve.

    • Ensure delivery quality, executive alignment, and measurable business impact.

    • Anticipate risks, unblock decisions, and help teams navigate ambiguity in high-stakes environments.

    • Bring senior judgment to moments where scope, resources, timelines, or expected value need to be clarified.

  • Build repeatable deployment excellence

    • Turn lessons from strategic engagements into reusable approaches, playbooks, and patterns.

    • Raise the bar for how AI programs are qualified, framed, delivered, and scaled.

    • Act as a senior relay for the Solutions organization in the region, helping teams adopt shared best practices, adapt them thoughtfully to local market specificities when needed, and strengthen the quality of execution.

    • Work hand in hand with Solutions leadership to connect customer realities, delivery patterns, and field feedback into practical ways of improving how Mistral deploys AI.

    • Help codify what great enterprise AI deployment looks like across industries and use cases.

    • Contribute to a Solutions culture that combines strategic clarity, technical depth, and strong execution.

  • Develop and multiply senior DS impact

    • Coach Deployment Strategists on strategic problem-solving, executive communication, and delivery leadership.

    • Help teams raise the quality of their work on the highest-impact opportunities.

    • Identify capability gaps and contribute to hiring, staffing, and development priorities.

    • Act as a force multiplier across accounts, teams, and regions where your experience can have the highest leverage.

 
 

What We're Looking For

 

You are a senior, highly capable professional with strong executive presence, excellent business judgment, and a track record of leading complex strategic or transformation work.

Typical indicators we’re looking for include:

  • 8–10+ years of professional experience in strategy consulting, digital transformation, AI, enterprise technology, or a similarly demanding environment.

  • Experience operating at Partner, Principal, Engagement Manager, Director, or equivalent level in a top-tier strategy consulting or transformation context.

  • A strong ability to structure ambiguous problems, identify value, and turn strategy into execution.

  • Experience leading large accounts, complex programs, or senior customer relationships.

  • The credibility to engage with executives and C-level stakeholders on business priorities, trade-offs, and impact.

  • Strong analytical and commercial judgment, with the ability to challenge assumptions constructively.

  • Comfort working at the frontier of technology, even when solutions are evolving quickly and the path is not fully defined.

  • A low-ego, high-ownership mindset and a desire to build with customers and teams, not just advise from a distance.

  • Fluency in English; German is a strong plus.

 

Hiring Process

 

• Talent Acquisition screening call

• 30min Hiring Manager Interview

• 45min Business Acumen Interview 

• 60min Technical Deep Dive on LLMs

• Panel (Home Prep & Restitution)

• 30min Value Talk

• Reference check

 

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.
